Cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin with his Matra Djet sports car in front of the Monument to the Conquerors of Space. Moscow 1965

Yuri Gagarin (March 9, 1934 – March 27, 1968) was a Russian Soviet pilot and cosmonaut. He was the first human to journey into outer space, when his Vostok spacecraft completed an orbit of the Earth on 12 April 1961.

The Monument to the Conquerors of Space is a monument erected in Moscow in 1964 to celebrate achievements of the Soviet people in space exploration. It depicts a starting rocket that rises on its exhaust plume. The monument is 110 meters (360.9 feet) tall, has 77° incline, and is made of titanium.

This Matra Bonnet Djet V S coupé is a French sports car that was apparently a gift to Gagarin from the French government, supposedly as a publicity stunt for the company.
